# dependencytrack_service_account_api_key (Resource)

Manages an API key of a Dependency-Track service account. Service account API keys always expire, and the plain text key is only returned when the key is created. API keys cannot be modified: changing any argument replaces the key. To rotate a key on a schedule, tie it to a `time_rotating` resource with `replace_triggered_by`. Requires Dependency-Track 5.2 or newer and the `ACCESS_MANAGEMENT` permission.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dependencytrack_service_account" "ci" {
  name = "ci-pipeline"
}

# Rotate the key every 30 days, ahead of its 60-day expiry.
resource "time_rotating" "ci_key" {
  rotation_days = 30
}

resource "dependencytrack_service_account_api_key" "ci" {
  service_account = dependencytrack_service_account.ci.name
  comment         = "GitHub Actions"
  expires_in_days = 60

  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [time_rotating.ci_key]
  }
}

output "ci_api_key" {
  value     = dependencytrack_service_account_api_key.ci.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `service_account` (String) The name of the service account the key belongs to (without the `svc:` prefix)

### Optional

- `comment` (String) A comment describing the key (max 255 characters)
- `expires_in_days` (Number) Number of days after creation when the key expires. Must not exceed the server's maximum key lifetime (`dt.api-key.max-lifetime-days`, 366 days by default). When unset, the server uses 30 days, or the maximum lifetime if that is shorter. Cannot be read back, so it is not set after import

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the key was created (RFC 3339)
- `expires_at` (String) When the key expires (RFC 3339)
- `id` (String) The ID of the API key in the format `service_account/public_id`
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The plain text API key. Only available when the key is created; null after import
- `public_id` (String) The public, non-secret part of the key

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Service account API keys can be imported using service_account/public_id.
# The plain text key cannot be read back, so `key` is null after import.
terraform import dependencytrack_service_account_api_key.example ci-pipeline/a1b2c3d4
```
